clue.text: Pay out money to get one's revenge?

explanation.surface: Someone paying out cash in order to even a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling accounts is both clearing debts with payment and, figuratively, getting even with an enemy.

clue.text: Location of the contents be fore being given thin cover age?

indicators.note: the printed 'coverage' tells us one word gives cover to, i.e. wraps around, another

parts.note: the printed 'before' means ere, an old word for earlier

explanation.surface: A question about where the contents of a package were before it got a flimsy wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: The page splits 'before' and 'coverage' in two; read whole, 'coverage' is the container signal, with 'being given' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein means 'in that place', which is where something's contents are found.

clue.text: Tortuous clue that's decidedly fishy

indicators.note: something tortuous is twisted, so the letters of the next word get twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A convoluted crossword clue that feels suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decidedly fishy' looks like it means suspicious, but here it is literal: a luce is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A luce is a pike, a freshwater fish, so the word is literally fishy.

clue.text: Mightily impressed about a GLO leader roused from GLC his slumbers?

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Mightily impressed about a GLO leader roused from GLC his slumbers?' (8): OCR 'GLO' should be GLC (Ken Livingstone, KEN in AWED with A) and a stray 'B' was misfiled as GLC, so the held clue cannot be quoted
annotationWithheld.clue: Mightily impressed about a GLO leader roused from GLC his slumbers?

clue.text: Miss Linton describing a country visited by Marco Polo

definitions.text: a country visited by Marco Polo

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one word goes around another

parts.note: Cathy Linton is a character in Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights

explanation.surface: A literary heroine telling of a land Marco Polo travelled to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' looks like telling about, but here it means drawing round, so CATHY goes around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathay is the old European name for China, where Marco Polo travelled.

clue.text: True rivals strangely beyond one's power

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of these words are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Real competitors who are oddly out of their depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra vires is the legal Latin term for an act outside the authority someone has.

clue.text: Dull sort of trash written re about in retrospect

indicators.note: about means around, so the mixed-up letters go around the other piece
sort of hints that the word is not quite itself, a rearranged version of it
looking back in retrospect says the short word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A remark about poor writing that looks dull when you look back on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 're' where the wordplay needs 'in'. 'sort of' makes TARSH, which 'about' wraps round the turned short word.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish metal is to make it lose its shine, to dull it.

clue.text: Sportingly conducted court action

parts.note: the court is not a law court but a sports court, and the action is a game played on it

explanation.definitionFit: A game played on a court with rackets is literally action on a court, done for sport.

clue.text: An inclination to write a litany, maybe

parts.note: to pen something is to write it
a litany is a chanted prayer, an example of a chant

explanation.surface: Someone with a fondness for composing prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a liking or tendency towards something.

clue.text: Compact clump of trees

indicators.note: a clump is a jumbled mass, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.walkthrough: 'clump of trees' reads as a stand of trees, but 'clump of' scrambles TREES.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse speech is brief and to the point, compact in words.

clue.text: Description of the holiday chalet in which Mme Bovary met her lover?

definitions.text: Description of the holiday chalet in which Mme Bovary met her lover?

parts.words: Description of the holiday chalet in which Mme Bovary met her lover?
parts.note: a garden pavilion used in the warm season, where in Flaubert's novel Emma Bovary had her trysts

explanation.definitionFit: A garden building used in the warm months is a light holiday-style retreat, the setting of Emma's meetings.

clue.text: Accustomed to being exploited, apparently

explanation.surface: Someone used to being taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Used to' means accustomed to, and to be used is to be taken advantage of.

clue.text: To a Persian it could be the parting of the ways

indicators.note: it could be says the letters could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A Persian traveller reaching a fork in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it could be' looks like a link, but it tells you to rearrange TO A PERSIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A separation is a split or parting, where two paths divide.

clue.text: The chief constable's ultimate deterrent?

parts.note: a senior police officer's last resort against disorder is bringing in physical power

explanation.definitionFit: Police use physical coercion only as a final measure to stop trouble.

clue.text: Government V IP in charge of the services?

explanation.surface: A senior politician who also runs church services.
explanation.definitionFit: A government department head and a clergyman who leads worship share the title.

clue.text: Decimal fractions

parts.note: 'decimal' read as one part in ten: the church levy took a tenth of produce

explanation.definitionFit: A tithe is a tenth of income paid to the church, so each one is a tenth part.

clue.text: When upset we notice what 2 is

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Something we spot when we get upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Two equals one doubled, so 2 is one multiplied by two.

clue.text: Why a 26 is 23?

indicators.note: the answer at 23 means misplaced, so the letters are put in other places

parts.note: the answer at 26, a Spanish gentleman

explanation.surface: A riddle asking why one entry is another.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is OUT OF PLACE and 26 is SENOR, so 'is 23' tells you to rearrange A + SENOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason is the cause of something, the answer to a 'why' question.

clue.text: Shakespeare character whose life an heroic female tried to save

definitions.text: Shakespeare character whose life an heroic female tried to save

parts.words: Shakespeare character whose life an heroic female tried to save
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice Portia, disguised as a lawyer, saves the merchant from Shylock

explanation.definitionFit: Portia defends the merchant of Venice in court to save his life from Shylock's bond.

clue.text: Tiny tapes twined round a climbing flower

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the mixed letters go around the other piece
twined means twisted together, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: wee is a Scottish word for tiny

explanation.surface: Small ribbons wound around a plant that climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiny tapes' looks like one phrase, but 'Tiny' is a separate piece set inside the rearranged STPEA, just after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a scented climbing plant grown in gardens.

clue.text: A spacious high-rise flat

parts.note: not an apartment in a tower but a wide stretch of level land that is high up

explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an expanse of level upland, broad, raised and flat.

clue.text: A team that looks as if it's 177

annotationWithheld.why: Printed 'A team that looks as if it's 177' (6): the OCR number '177' is garbled and no scan or search gives the original
annotationWithheld.clue: A team that looks as if it's 177

clue.text: Not employed in the wrong position?

explanation.surface: Someone jobless and feeling they don't belong.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of a job is having no place; being misplaced is being in the wrong spot.

clue.text: Refuse to make brandy

explanation.definitionFit: Marc is the leftover skins after grapes are pressed, and also the spirit distilled from them.

clue.text: Feature of a ship providing ground-nuts for pigs

explanation.surface: A ship's part that also feeds swine.
explanation.definitionFit: A mast holds a ship's sails; beech and oak nuts fallen on the ground, eaten by pigs, are also called mast.

clue.text: A coin of little value to a Japanese or a Spaniard

parts.words: A coin of little value to a Japanese
parts.note: the sen was a small Japanese coin worth a hundredth of a yen

explanation.surface: A cheap coin that means as much to a Japanese as to a Spaniard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or a Spaniard' looks like a second recipient, but 'or' gives letters and 'a Spaniard' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Senor is the Spanish form of address for a man, used for a Spanish gentleman.

clue.text: Sort of dovetail put to fane use

indicators.note: sort of says the letters are a different arrangement of the next word

explanation.surface: A woodworking joint used for something irreverent.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'fane' is OCR debris for 'profane'; the definition is 'put to profane use'.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate a sacred place is to desecrate it, treating it irreverently.

clue.text: Economies that are forced on people from Westminster?

definitions.text: Economies that are forced on people from Westminster?

parts.words: Economies that are forced on people from Westminster?
parts.note: Westminster stands for Parliament, and the economies are spending reductions imposed by it

explanation.definitionFit: Spending reductions imposed by those in power on the public are savings decreed from Parliament.
